facts.claim: A DAX cluster consists of exactly one primary node and between zero and ten read replica nodes.
facts.quote: A DAX cluster consists of exactly one primary node, and between zero and ten read replica nodes.

facts.claim: A DAX cluster can support up to 11 nodes per cluster: the primary node plus a maximum of 10 read replicas.
facts.quote: A DAX cluster can support up to 11 nodes per cluster (the primary node plus a maximum of 10 read replicas).

facts.claim: The default TTL for each of the DAX caches (item cache and query cache) is 5 minutes. You can use a custom parameter group to set different TTL settings.
facts.quote: The default TTL for each of these caches is 5 minutes. If you want to use different TTL settings, you can launch a DAX cluster using a custom parameter group.

facts.claim: DAX provides access to eventually consistent data from DynamoDB tables with microsecond latency, and a Multi-AZ DAX cluster can serve millions of requests per second.
facts.quote: DAX provides access to eventually consistent data from DynamoDB tables, with microsecond latency. A Multi-AZ DAX cluster can serve millions of requests per second.

facts.claim: For use cases that need response times in microseconds, DynamoDB integrates with DAX, a fully managed, highly available caching service built for DynamoDB.
facts.quote: For use cases that require response times in microseconds, DynamoDB integrates with Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX), a fully managed, highly available caching service built for DynamoDB.

facts.claim: DAX is a fully managed, highly available caching service built for DynamoDB. It delivers up to a 10 times performance improvement, from milliseconds to microseconds, even at millions of requests per second.
facts.quote: DAX delivers up to a 10 times performance improvement—from milliseconds to microseconds—even at millions of requests per second.

facts.claim: DAX is described as ideal for applications that need the fastest possible read response time and for applications that read a small number of items more frequently than others, such as a hot key during a one-day sale.
facts.quote: Applications that require the fastest possible response time for reads.

facts.claim: DAX does the heavy lifting of in-memory acceleration without requiring developers to manage cache invalidation, data population or cluster management. Because DAX is compatible with existing DynamoDB API calls, AWS says no application logic modification is required.
facts.quote: DAX does all the heavy lifting required to add in-memory acceleration to your DynamoDB tables, without requiring developers to manage cache invalidation, data population, or cluster management. As DAX is compatible with existing DynamoDB API calls, no application logic modification is required.

facts.claim: DAX is not ideal for applications that do not require microsecond response times for reads or that do not need to offload repeated read activity from the underlying tables.
facts.quote: Applications that do not require microsecond response times for reads, or that do not need to offload repeated read activity from underlying tables.

facts.claim: DAX is not ideal for applications that require strongly consistent reads, for write-intensive applications, or for applications without many repeated reads. DAX performs best when cache hit rates exceed 90%.
facts.quote: Applications that require strongly consistent reads (or that cannot tolerate eventually consistent reads).
